generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: GOOGLE INTRODUCES GENIE 4
Summary: Genie 4 is a world model that generates photorealistic, interactive environments with synchronized audio and real-time prompt-based editing. It can maintain consistent simulations for up to two minutes, doubling Genie 3's duration, while improving physics and character realism.

Editorial idea:
A generated world becomes convincing only when its rules remain coherent while the viewer changes it.

Central subject:
An interactive simulated environment being reshaped by a human prompt

Visual relationship:
The scene must hold together across movement, sound, physics, and edits, showing the tension between instant generation and sustained consistency.

Composition:
A continuous landscape viewed at eye level, with one side freshly transforming into a new configuration while the rest remains stable; a visible path through the environment connects the unchanged and edited regions without using interface text or decorative technology imagery.

Permitted literal elements:
A photorealistic interactive landscape
A clear transition between stable and newly edited terrain
Consistent lighting and physical continuity across the scene
Subtle visual evidence of synchronized environmental change

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
Racks
Chips
Laptops
Robots
Clouds
Shields
Arrows
Charts
Skyscrapers
Chess
Handshakes
Split-screen conflict
Rendered text
Logos
Artist imitation
Unsupported physical details

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Depicting a generic virtual-reality scene without showing interactive editing
Showing a static generated landscape rather than a changing environment
Using futuristic interface overlays or unreadable text as the main idea
Making the edited and unchanged areas look like unrelated scenes

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
